attempts.summary: node1 (SONiC) was given routed addresses on its two segments — eth1=192.168.11.1/24 toward node2, eth2=192.168.12.1/24 toward node3 — with IPv4 forwarding enabled, establishing a working L3 path between node2 (192.168.11.2) and node3 (192.168.12.2) through node1. Because SONiC's `config` CLI only manages abstracted Ethernet* ports (not real eth1/eth2 host NICs) and the boot-time reconcilers (interfaces-config.service/networking.service) only touch eth0, persistence required static stanzas in /etc/network/interfaces.d/, sysctl.d for forwarding, and — after discovering a periodic SONiC daemon transiently stripped the addresses shortly after boot — a self-healing systemd watchdog ([REDACTED].service, enabled, Restart=always, re-applies every 5s) that keeps the addressing and forwarding in place indefinitely. node2 and node3 got static eth1 addresses and cross-segment routes via node1, persisted through NetworkManager connection profiles. All three nodes were restarted one at a time using native reboot; each showed a changed boot_id post-restart and post-recovery checks confirmed addressing, routes, forwarding, and end-to-end node2<->node3 connectivity all returned automatically with no manual intervention.
